title: Filesystem race classes
description: One closed table that classifies a raw filesystem error (ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EISDIR, ESTALE, ELOOP, and on Windows the sharing violations EBUSY, EPERM, EACCES) raised by a READ of a path inside the workspace while peers edit the tree. The classification is made once, at the two boundaries of the churn policy (the layer that retries a snapshot and the process that restarts a command) and for the text of a failed child: `transient` (a vanished or stale path is present again, or a path is only busy: read it again), `persistent` (the path is gone, or a directory or symlink took the place of the file, and a directory around it changed since this process started: only a new snapshot or a new process cures it), `none` (not a race: the error stands). A path is only suspected when a witness agrees: the nearest existing directory above it was modified after this process started (minus the slack), so a typo in a stable directory fails at once.
